definitions.explanation: Indicates likelihood or probability. Suggests the speaker thinks something is likely but isn't certain.

examples.japanese: たぶん{明日|あした}は{雨|あめ}でしょう。
たぶん{大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}だと{思|おも}います。
たぶん{来|こ}ないと{思|おも}います。
examples.english: I don't think they'll probably come.

examples.japanese: 「{田中|たなか}さんは{来|き}ますか。」「たぶん{来|く}ると{思|おも}いますが、わかりません。」
examples.english: "Will Tanaka-san come?" "I think they'll probably come, but I'm not sure."

examples.japanese: たぶん{電車|でんしゃ}が{遅|おく}れたのでしょう。いつもは{時間|じかん}どおりに{来|く}る{人|ひと}ですから。
examples.english: The train was probably delayed. They're usually someone who arrives on time.

notes: たぶん can be written in kanji as {多分|たぶん}. It's often used with でしょう or と{思|おも}う to express uncertainty. Similar to きっと (surely/certainly) but たぶん expresses less certainty. おそらく is a more formal synonym.
